_note: The intro (src/ui/intro.ts): the card the page opens on, which is also the loading screen, and the shorter one that plays as you drop into a match. Black screen, green rain falling at a different speed in every column, the name smashed in over it, then a rifle round through the middle: the glass cracks from a bullet hole, a beat of quiet, and then one shotgun blast puts a spread of holes through the whole pane at once before it lets go and falls away into the game. The beats are seconds from the start and each is the moment it begins, so they read in order; `blast` is the shotgun, `out` is when the shards start falling and `end` is when the card is gone. The boot card holds on the rain until the world is in (`waitMost` seconds at the outside), so it covers loading rather than being shown after it; the match one plays over a match that is already starting underneath, so it is short and never in the way. Every beat is skipped by a key or a click, and with `prefers-reduced-motion` the shake, the flash and the falling shards are dropped for a plain fade (`reduced`).

reduced._note: No shake, no flash, no shards: the card fades in, holds, cracks once and fades out.

text._note: The card's own words. `mark` is the big line and `sub` the one under it, spaced out the way a game's title screen spaces it.

rain._note: The green rainfall. A column is `column` pixels wide, its glyphs `glyph` pixels tall, and it falls at somewhere between `slow` and `fast` glyphs a second, drawn afresh every `swap` seconds so the characters change as they fall. `trail` is how much of the last frame is kept (the tail behind each head), `head` how bright the leading glyph is and `dim` the rest.
rain.head: #d9ffe4

crack._note: The first shot through the screen. `rays` cracks run out from the hole, each wandering by up to `wander` radians; `rings` are the rings of glass between them, the ones that make it read as a pane rather than a star. `hole` is the bullet hole's radius in pixels and `spread` how many seconds the cracks take to run to the edge. `shake` is the screen's kick in pixels at the moment of the shot. `flash` is how white the screen goes at the shot, 0..1: 0.45, half of the 0.9 it was, because the owner found the flashes too bright.

wait._note: The boot card holds on the rain and the name until the world is in, so the animation covers loading instead of following it. `waitMost` is the longest it will hold before it fires anyway, because a card that never ends is worse than a card that fires early.

_settle: The card lets the page load first (the owner, 2026-09-27: "the loading screens with the matrix lag ... slowly fading in or letting it load first"). Measured (tools/intro-frames.ts): the boot card froze for 2.9 s, 1.0 s and 0.3 s in its first two seconds while the world loaded under it, and the match card for two 0.8 s spells that swallowed its title, shot and blast, because it animates on the page's own thread. So it opens on a still: its frame, the name faint and the loading line, faded in over `fade` s by the browser's compositor (which keeps going while the page is busy). It starts only when `frames` frames in a row have each come within `under` ms or `spike` times the median of the last few (so a slow machine is calm too, and only a stall holds it), and counted only once the world is in on the boot card (and in SpeedKills the bought guns dressed, the soldier's clips carried over and the first-person arms built, each a stall of 0.3 to 0.5 s that had landed on the card after it began); never later than `holdMost` s (boot, match). `pixels` caps the canvas at about that many pixels (at 2x a 1920 by 1080 screen it filled 8.3 million a frame). After: the boot card's longest frame 25 ms (was 2867 ms, with five over 100 ms), the match card's one of 110 to 125 ms in its fade out as the match's first frames show through (was two of 829 ms).

blast._note: The shotgun blast that finishes the pane: one flash, one kick, and `pellets` holes through the glass in the same instant, thrown out over `spread` of the screen and never into the middle (`keepOut` of the way out, so the pattern is round the name rather than over it, and the rifle round's own hole stays the one in the centre). Each pellet is a smaller hole than the rifle round's with `rays` short cracks at `reach` of its length, so the first shot stays the break that carries the pane. One blast reads as a shotgun; a string of single rounds read as a strobe, which is what this replaced. `flashAlpha` is how white the blast turns the screen, 0..1, and `flash` how long it lasts, s: 0.375, half of the 0.75 it was.

_modes: The card that plays as a match starts is the same animation with the mode's own words: `name` is the big line, the mode's name, and `sub` the line under it. The game's own name goes small above them, so every card is still ours. The key is the kind of match (src/game/stats.ts MatchKind; every bot difficulty is `bots`), and a battle royale on Resurgence rules is `resurgence`. A kind not listed plays the boot card's words.
_speedkills: SpeedKills' own card (src/game/game.ts): its name as the big line, its line under it, and the rain in its two neon colours instead of the green.
_matchHold: SpeedKills holds a match's start while its mode card plays (main.ts, duel.ts LocalState.held): at the most this many seconds from the card's start, whatever happens to it. The card runs on the browser's animation frames, and a tab in the background gets none: the card stood still, its player was never ready, and the match (every friend in it) waited for ever (Milestone 348's live check). The card is 1.85 s and settles for 4 at the most, so 8 never cuts one short. A tab that goes into the background skips its card besides.
_show: SpeedKills' way into a match (main.ts show): the loading screen up again with `text` as its line while the match's own files come in (the bought guns' textures for the loot and the bots, 62 files on the first battle royale of a page) and `loadFrames` frames in a row after that come steadily (a few: the range is what is drawn under it, and a page drawn in software never gave settle.frames of them), `loadMost` s at the most (1 to 2 s on a fast machine; a page drawn in software in the e2e took the whole of 20); a battle royale then starts under it, you are put on the ship and the ship waits at its start until the frames there are steady too, `boardMost` s at the most from the match's start (the first frames on that side of the world were a black frame with the gun and a 300 ms stall on a fast machine, between the card and the ship: the owner, 2026-09-30); then the mode's card, and the match or the ship only once it has gone. While a friend's match waits for the others (still loading, or on the menu), the line says `waitText`. The menu opened over it (Esc) puts the screen aside once it has been open `menuGrace` s (the click that starts a match takes the pointer a frame or two late). As Start is clicked the screen goes up before the match is built, the build waiting two frames and `paintWait` s more: the frame that shows the screen is only on the monitor once the GPU has put it there, and a build begun on the next frame kept the GPU busy, so the menu stood through the whole build in the frame capture.

show.waitText: WAITING FOR THE OTHERS TO BE READY
show._city: A match on the Neon City waits for its file and its shaders under its screen (the city is not loaded with the page: main.ts askCity): `cityText` and the megabytes while it comes, `cityUnpack` and the textures done while its file is unpacked (its 728 compressed textures turned into what the GPU reads, and its geometry decompressed: two seconds and more after its last byte, when the screen sat on the full megabytes and looked stuck, the owner 2026-10-03), `cityReady` while its shaders are built, and `cityMost` seconds at the most (its file is 75 to 349 MB by the preset). The unpacking runs on `cityWorkers` workers at the most (one fewer than the machine's processors, and no fewer than three's own four): three's pool of four took 2.1 s for the 728.
show._warmSliceMs: The city's shaders are built a slice a frame, `warmSliceMs` of the frame's time at the most (main.ts warmBrSide), the screen saying how many of them are done: all at once they held the page over a second the frame the city came in, the bar standing still (2026-10-03).
show._cardMin: The battle royale's player card is up at least `cardMin` seconds from Start, however soon the match is ready, the ship held at its start until then (the owner, 2026-10-03: at least 5 s; on a quick load it went by before it could be read).
